questions.question: When and where was Elsa Brita Heikkinen, christened 16 June 1832 in Iisalmi, Kuopio, Finland, born?
questions.rationale: This is the objective restated as its single-fact question. Elsa has a well-sourced christening entry in the Finland Baptisms collection (Iisalmi parish, 16 June 1832) but no birth date or specific birth place is recorded on the tree. Finnish Lutheran baptism registers from this period routinely recorded the birth date alongside the christening entry in the same register line, so the original parish register for Iisalmi circa 1832 is the primary record set to search.

search_stop.justification: The autonomous agent exhausted its tool capability before completing the full repository breadth required for this question. FamilySearch Catalog 4110832 (Iisalmi Kirkonkirjat 1747–1870, 528 images) was attempted (log_015) but all image-transcription calls returned HTTP 403 — access is restricted to FamilySearch Centers. The three external Finnish portals named in the research plan (HisKi at hiski.genealogia.fi, SSHY Digiarkisto at sukuhistoria.fi/sshy, and the Finnish National Archives Digitaaliarkisto at digi.narc.fi) are not in the URL-builder tool's supported-site list and require a human to navigate; they were documented for researcher follow-up (log_016) but never actually searched. These portals hold the original Iisalmi baptism register — the decisive record that would supply the specific birth date and satisfy evidence_class (original, primary information) and independent_verification (a second independent source). Until at least one of these portals is searched by the researcher, independent_verification (criterion 4) and evidence_class (criterion 5) cannot be met, and repository_breadth (criterion 2) remains incomplete.

(3) Finnish National Archives Digitaaliarkisto (digi.narc.fi) — digitized Iisalmi parish records (Iisalmen seurakunnan arkisto); select the baptism register series covering 1832 and read the Syntymäpäivä / Född column for Elsa Brita, village Kilpisaari. items.rationale: The 'Finland, Baptisms, 1657-1890' collection is name-searchable and is already cited on the tree for Elsa Brita's christening (ARKs XBFJ-HS6, XBFJ-HSF, XBFJ-HSX for the christening date 16 Jun 1832), but no birth date was extracted from those index entries. A targeted name search — Elsa Brita Heickinen / Heikkinen, Iisalmi, 1832 — should surface the full indexed record and expose whatever birth-date field the index captured alongside the christening date. Per loc_001, Heikkinen appears as 'Heickin' and Pardanen as 'Pardain' in period Swedish-language registers; both spellings must be tried. Per loc_001, this collection is index-only with no embedded register images; the original image is addressed in pli_004.

The 'Finland, Church Census and Pre-Confirmation Books, 1600-1916' collection is name-searchable and includes the Iisalmi lastenkirjat (children's pre-confirmation books). Volume_search confirms two lastenkirja volumes for Iisalmi cover this period: I Ab:6 (1827-1839, imageGroup 102151589) and I Ab:7 (1821-1839, imageGroup 102151590). The lastenkirja records each child's birth date and home village — the two pieces of information the question seeks — making this potentially the most direct source. Per loc_001, children under confirmation age (~14-16) appear in the lastenkirja rather than the communion books; a child christened June 1832 would be enrolled here through approximately 1846-1848. Search under Elsa Brita Heickinen / Heikkinen and her father And Joh Heickin, Iisalmi.

FAN item — read the indexed baptism entries for Elsa Brita's two siblings already in the tree: Christina Heikkinen (christened 26 May 1827, ARK XBFK-3C3) and David Heikkinen (christened 11 Apr 1830, ARK XBFV-X4F), both children of And Joh Heikkinen + Lisa Pardanen in the 'Finland, Baptisms, 1657-1890' collection. The village field in their entries is the best available proxy for Elsa Brita's home village in 1832, since the family would not have moved between 1827 and 1832. Reading these records also confirms how the parents' names appear in the register (Swedish spelling variants) and cross-checks the parent identification for Elsa Brita against the viable parent pair — the only biologically possible pairing of the competing tree sets, given that LZRL-9DT (Maria Eskelinen) died 2 Feb 1826 and cannot be Elsa's mother.

If the name search in the baptism index (pli_001) does not yield the birth date — per loc_001 the 'Finland, Baptisms, 1657-1890' collection is index-only, with actual register images held in the FamilySearch Catalog — browse the original Iisalmi baptism register images via FamilySearch Catalog item 4110832 (Kirkonkirjat 1747-1870). This is browse-only (personCount 0) at the image-group level. Navigate to the June 1832 section and read the birth-date column directly from the register page. The register is in Swedish; look for 'Elsa Brita' under the father's entry 'And Joh Heickin' and mother 'Lisa Pardain' (name forms per loc_001). The original register typically records the birth date and christening date in separate columns, so this step is expected to supply the birth date even if the index omitted it.

If FamilySearch Catalog images (pli_004) are inaccessible or the June 1832 folios are damaged, search three external Finnish genealogy portals: (1) HisKi Project (hiski.genealogia.fi) — the Genealogical Society of Finland's index of Iisalmi parish births, which may transcribe the birth date from the original register; loc_001 notes HisKi's Iisalmi coverage is incomplete, so a negative result does not rule out the record. (2) SSHY (digiarkisto.org/sshy or www.sukuhistoria.fi/sshy) — browse-only original Iisalmi church book images. (3) Finnish National Archives ASTIA portal (astia.narc.fi) — digitized register images not available on FamilySearch. The Ancestry mirror 'Finland Select Baptisms, 1657-1890' (ancestry.com) is the same underlying index as FamilySearch's collection and need not be searched separately unless the FamilySearch index record is incomplete.

hypotheses.claim: Elsa Brita Heikkinen (M76V-5PF) is the daughter of And Joh Heikkinen (KCGT-RPC) and Lisa Pardanen (KHGS-4YL)
hypotheses.notes: Supported by the three indexed baptism ARKs for Elsa Brita herself (XBFJ-HS6, XBFJ-HSF, XBFJ-HSX, read in log_004–log_006), all of which name 'and Joh Heikkinen' as father and 'Lisa Pardanen' as mother. No assertions were extracted from those ARKs in the a_001–a_023 range. Corroborated by the sibling baptism records for Christina (src_001, a_004–a_010) and David (src_002, a_014–a_020), which show the same parents in the same Iisalmi parish. Further corroborated by the pre-confirmation book entry for Elsa Brita herself (src_003, a_021–a_023, ARK QLVK-ZPHR). The project objective explicitly names this parent pair. proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Birth of Elsa Brita Heikkinen, Iisalmi, Kuopio, Finland

**Research Question:** When and where was Elsa Brita Heikkinen, christened 16 June 1832 in Iisalmi, Kuopio, Finland, born?

**Conclusion:** The available evidence supports, at a possible tier, that Elsa Brita Heikkinen (FamilySearch ID M76V-5PF) was born in May 1832 at Kilpisaari, Iisalmen maalaiskunta, Kuopio, Finland — the parish village where the family is documented in a church census book — and was christened approximately six weeks later, on 16 June 1832, at the Iisalmen maalaiskunta church. The conclusion rests on a single derivative source of indeterminate informant quality; the original Iisalmi baptism register, which would supply the exact birth day and directly state the birth village, has not yet been examined by the researcher.

### Evidence and Source Classification

**The pre-confirmation church census book (src_003).** The key record is: "Finland, Church Census and Pre-Confirmation Books, 1600-1916," *FamilySearch* (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QLVK-ZPHR : Mon Dec 08 12:32:05 UTC 2025), Entry for Elsa Brita Heickinen, from 1851 to 1860.

This is a **derivative** source — a compiled register index, not the original register entry. It records Elsa Brita Heickinen's birth as "May 1832" and places the household at Kilpisaari, Iisalmen maalaiskunta, Kuopio, Suomi during the census period 1851 to 1860. The informant for the birth date is unknown; Finnish pre-confirmation books did not systematically record who supplied household information, so the information quality is classified as **indeterminate**. Pre-confirmation books were maintained by parish clergy and typically compiled birth dates from original baptism registers, so the recorded month may reflect the underlying register or may reflect a later household recollection. The name "Heickinen" is a documented period variant of "Heikkinen" in Swedish-language Iisalmi records, and Kilpisaari is within Iisalmi parish. The identification of this record with Elsa Brita Heikkinen (M76V-5PF) is confident (FamilySearch match score 0.8064; name variant, birth month, and parish all consistent with the known christening entry).

**Corroboration from the christening date.** The FamilySearch index of the Iisalmi baptism register (ARKs XBFJ-HS6, XBFJ-HSF, and XBFJ-HSX — three personas of the same underlying record, MPS4-2SY) confirms that Elsa Brita was christened on 16 June 1832 in Iisalmen mlk, Kuopio, Finland, with father "and Joh Heikkinen" and mother "Lisa Pardanen." The index captured only the christening date; the original register images — which would show the birth date in the "Född" column — are not accessible online (HTTP 403, center-only). The gap of approximately six weeks between a May 1832 birth and the 16 June 1832 christening is consistent with Finnish Lutheran practice, in which infants were commonly christened four to six weeks after birth. This independently corroborates "May 1832" as the birth month without itself establishing it.

**Sibling baptism records (src_001 and src_002).** Two sibling christening entries in the FamilySearch Finland Baptisms index establish the family's continuous presence in Iisalmi parish:

- Christina Heikkinen, christened 26 May 1827, Iisalmen mlk: "Finland, Baptisms, 1657-1890", , *FamilySearch* (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:MPS4-Z75 : 23 June 2020), Entry for Christina, 1827. Father "and Joh Heikkinen," mother "Lisa Pardanen."
- David Heikkinen, christened 11 Apr 1830, Iisalmen mlk: "Finland, Baptisms, 1657-1890", , *FamilySearch* (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:MPS4-66Z : 23 June 2020), Entry for David, 1830. Same parents.

Both are **derivative** sources (FamilySearch index entries); the informant in each is the presenting parent, classified as **primary** information for the child named in that record. These records index location only at the rural municipality level (Iisalmen mlk) and do not supply Elsa Brita's birth date or the family's specific home village. Their value for this conclusion is family-identity context: they confirm that And Joh Heikkinen (KCGT-RPC) and Lisa Pardanen (KHGS-4YL) were resident in Iisalmi parish from at least 1827 to 1830, placing the family in the parish where Elsa Brita was christened in 1832.

### Birth Place Assessment

The pre-confirmation book entry's "Kilpisaari, Iisalmen maalaiskunta" is the census residence location for 1851–1860, not a directly stated birth place. Assertion a_023 (birth "May 1832") carries no place; the place derives from assertion a_022 (census, Kilpisaari), both from the same underlying record. The inference that Kilpisaari was also the birth location is reasonable — the family was documented there during the pre-confirmation period and had christened children in Iisalmi parish since at least 1827 — but remains indirect. The original Iisalmi baptism register contained a separate "Född" (born) column that would directly state the birth village; until that register is examined, "Kilpisaari" is the best available but inferential birth place.

### Competing Parent Hypotheses

Three parent-pair hypotheses were evaluated for the family. Hypotheses h_002 (Anders Johan Heikkinen L83L-TYW + Maria Daviddr Eskelinen LZRL-9DT) and h_003 (Anders Johan Heikkinen L89R-XVF + LZRL-9DT) were ruled out: Maria Daviddr Eskelinen (LZRL-9DT) died 2 February 1826, making her biological motherhood of a child christened 16 June 1832 a chronological impossibility. Hypothesis h_001 — parentage of And Joh Heikkinen (KCGT-RPC) and Lisa Pardanen (KHGS-4YL) — is supported by all three sources consulted.

### Research Scope and Limitations

The FamilySearch Finland Baptisms, 1657–1890 derivative index was searched, including Elsa Brita's own baptism ARKs and her siblings' records. The FamilySearch Church Census and Pre-Confirmation Books, 1600–1916 collection was searched by subject name and yielded the key record. Pre-confirmation book image groups 102151589 and 102151590 (Iisalmi lastenkirja volumes) were searched by surname but returned no indexed results for the target family, likely because the father may have been indexed under a patronymic variant. FamilySearch Catalog item 4110832 (Kirkonkirjat 1747–1870, 528 images) returned HTTP 403 for all image access — center-only restriction. Not reached in the autonomous research session: the original Iisalmi baptism register at a FamilySearch Center (Catalog 4110832); the HisKi text-transcription index at hiski.genealogia.fi (Iisalmi Kastetut, year 1832); SSHY Digiarkisto at sukuhistoria.fi/sshy; and the Finnish National Archives Digitaaliarkisto at digi.narc.fi. Each of these resources holds access to the original 1832 Iisalmi baptism register and is accessible to a human researcher. Examining any one of them would supply the exact birth day within May 1832 and the birth village as directly stated in the register, which would support advancing the conclusion to `probable` or higher.

### Tier Declaration

This conclusion is offered at the **possible** tier. A single derivative source of indeterminate informant quality supports the birth month and year; the birth place is inferred from the same record's census residence rather than directly stated in the birth entry; and the original Iisalmi baptism register — which would settle both the exact birth day and the birth village — remains unsearched. The conclusion may be advanced to `probable` or higher once the original register is examined at a FamilySearch Center or through HisKi, SSHY Digiarkisto, or the Finnish National Archives Digitaaliarkisto.

quirks: All Iisalmi church records for 1800-1850 are written in Swedish, not Finnish. Finnish was not the official language until 1863. Names appear in Swedish spelling or abbreviation (e.g., Heikkinen appears as Heickin or Heickin in period records; Pardanen appears as Pardain).

Iisalmi is in eastern Finland (Kuopio county), where children under confirmation age (~14-16) were NOT recorded in the communion books (rippikirjat). They appear instead in the pre-confirmation books (lastenkirjat/barnböcker). For a child christened in 1832, search the lastenkirjat through approximately 1846-1848, not the rippikirjat.
Iisalmi uses eastern Finnish fixed family surnames (ending in -nen, e.g., Heikkinen), not patronymics. The surname stays the same across generations, unlike western Finnish practice.

The FamilySearch 'Finland Baptisms' collection (1778464) is an index only — it does not include images. For the actual register images, use the FamilySearch Catalog entries (Kirkonkirjat 1747-1870, catalog 4110832; Kirkonkirjat 1664-1950, catalog 3044), the Finnish National Archives ASTIA portal (astia.narc.fi), or Digihakemisto (digihakemisto.net).

The HisKi index at hiski.genealogia.fi covers Iisalmi parish births but is incomplete. A name-search hit there is useful, but a negative result does not mean the record is absent — check the original images.

Lapinlahti parish was separated from Iisalmi in 1821. Families living in the area that became Lapinlahti appear in Iisalmi records before that year and in Lapinlahti records after. If the family's village is near the Lapinlahti boundary, check both parishes.

The surrounding parishes (clockwise from north) are: Vierema, Sonkajärvi, Lapinlahti, Maaninka, Pielavesi, and Kiuruvesi — all in Kuopio County. Families near those borders may appear in neighbouring parish registers.

FamilySearch does not hold records from the Orthodox congregation (ortodoksinen kirkko) in Iisalmi. If the family was Orthodox, records are not on FamilySearch; contact the Orthodox Diocese of Kuopio and Karelia.
localities.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Iisalmi Parish, Kuopio, Finland (1800–1850)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** The parish of Iisalmi was formed in 1620–1627 from Kuopio parish and originally covered the entire Ylä-Savo (Upper Savonia) area. (FamilySearch Wiki: [Iisalmi Parish, Kuopio, Finland Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Iisalmi_Parish,_Kuopio,_Finland_Genealogy))
- **County seat / administrative center:** Iisalmi town (gained town status in 1891; during 1800–1850 it was a rural parish center)
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Kuopio County (Lääni), historical province of Savonia (Maakunta)
- **Population during period:** Population data from the tools was not returned for this specific parish; Iisalmi was a large rural parish in the Upper Savonia region.
- **Economy:** Agriculture and small-scale rural crafts; the region is heavily forested lake-country.
- **Ethnic composition:** Almost entirely ethnic Finns; Finnish-speaking with Swedish used only in church and official records.
- **Religious denominations:** Evangelical Lutheran (the state church, which kept all vital records). An Orthodox congregation also existed but FamilySearch holds no Orthodox records for Iisalmi. There are no Catholic or other denomination records for this period.
- **Key historical events:** Finland passed from Sweden to Russia as the Grand Duchy of Finland in 1809, immediately before the target period. Record-keeping practices remained Lutheran-church-centered and changed little under Russian administration. In 1821, Lapinlahti was separated out as its own parish from Iisalmi.

## Boundary changes
- **Original territory (pre-1800):** At its formation the parish included the entire Ylä-Savo region. By 1800 several parishes — Kiuruvesi, Lapinlahti, Pielavesi, Sonkajärvi, and Vierema — had already been or were being separated out.
- **1821 – Lapinlahti separation:** Lapinlahti was formally constituted as its own parish. Families in villages that fell into the new Lapinlahti parish appear in Iisalmi registers before 1821 and in Lapinlahti registers from 1821 onward. Researchers must know which village a family lived in to determine which side of this boundary they were on.
- **Judicial district changes (relevant to court records):** Iisalmi district (Iisalmen tuomiokunta) was operative from 1723; the preceding district was Pien-Savon ylinen (1796–1821). Court records accordingly span multiple district names across the period.
- **1832 status:** At the time of Elsa Brita Heikkinen's christening in June 1832, Iisalmi was a single, still-large rural parish in Kuopio County. Record-keeping was at the parish level by the Lutheran clergy. There was no civil registration.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Status for 1800–1850:** There was no state civil registration in Finland during this period. The Evangelical Lutheran Church was the state church and its registers ARE the vital records. Civil registration began only in 1923 for those outside the church (and the general population register fully replaced church records only in 1971). ([Finland Civil Registration](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Finland_Civil_Registration))
- **What to use instead:** The Lutheran parish's christening/baptism register (syntyneet ja kastetut) is the primary vital record for births. These are detailed below under Church Records.

### Church records
This is the central record class for 1800–1850 Iisalmi. All records are held at the parish level (not town or county level); the clergy created them and they are now digitized at FamilySearch and the Finnish National Archives.

**Denominations present:** Evangelical Lutheran (overwhelmingly dominant); Orthodox congregation (not covered by FamilySearch). ([Iisalmi Parish, Kuopio, Finland Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Iisalmi_Parish,_Kuopio,_Finland_Genealogy#Church_Records))

**Language:** All records through 1863 are written in Swedish, not Finnish. Finnish names appear in their Swedish equivalents or abbreviated forms. For example, the surname Heikkinen appears in period records as "Heickin" or "Heickin"; Pardanen appears as "Pardain". ([Finland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Finland_Church_Records))

#### Christening / baptism registers (Syntyneet ja kastetut / Födelselängder och doplängder)
- **What exists:** Iisalmi Lutheran christening registers survive from 1657. For the target period 1800–1850 they are complete and well-preserved.
- **Content:** The register line for each child typically records: child's name, christening date, birth date (later registers), father's name and occupation, mother's name, farm/village of residence, and the names of godparents/witnesses. Earlier registers (early 1800s) may give less detail on birth date or mother's name. ([Finland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Finland_Church_Records#Births))
- **Digitization:** **Indexed + images available.** The national collection [Finland, Baptisms, 1657-1890](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1778464) (FamilySearch collection 1778464, 4.5 million records) includes Iisalmi and is name-searchable. However, this collection is an **index only** — it does not include images of the original registers. For the actual register images, use:
  - [Kirkonkirjat, 1747-1870](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/4110832) (Iisalmen maalaiskunta) — FamilySearch Catalog, browse-only images
  - [Kirkonkirjat, 1664-1950](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/3044) (Iisalmen maalaiskunta) — FamilySearch Catalog, browse-only images
  - Finnish National Archives ASTIA portal: [astia.narc.fi](https://astia.narc.fi/uusiastia/) — records from 1527 to 100 years ago
  - [Digihakemisto](https://digihakemisto.net/) — images
  - SSHY (Finland's Family History Association): [digiarkisto.org/sshy](https://www.digiarkisto.org/sshy/index_eng.htm) — images
- Also mirrored at Ancestry ([Finland Select Baptisms, 1657-1890](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/9863)) and MyHeritage ([Finland Baptisms, 1657-1890](https://www.myheritage.com/research/collection-30233/finland-baptisms-1657-1890)) (subscription required).

#### Communion books (Rippikirjat / Kommunionböcker)
- **What they are:** Periodic household-by-household surveys of all confirmed parish members, recording birth dates, birthplaces, marriage and death dates, and moving information. They function as a detailed census of the parish.
- **Critical eastern Finland quirk:** Iisalmi is in eastern Finland, where children under confirmation age (approximately 14–16) were **NOT** included in the rippikirjat. They appear instead in the pre-confirmation books (lastenkirjat, below). A child christened in June 1832 would not appear in the communion books until confirmation, expected around 1846–1848.
- **FamilySearch volumes for 1800–1850 (from volume_search):**
  - Rippikirjat, Aa:9 (1805–1815) — image group 102151575, 489 images, 97% indexed
  - Rippikirjat, Aa:10 (1807–1815) — image group 102151576, 172 images, 97% indexed
  - Rippikirjat, Aa:11 (1816–1826) — image group 102151577, 369 images, 98% indexed
  - Rippikirjat, Aa:12 (1816–1826) — image group 102151578, 358 images, 98% indexed
  - Rippikirjat, Aa:13 (1827–1837) — image group 102151579, 499 images, 96% indexed
  - Rippikirjat, Aa:14 (1827–1837) — image group 102151580, 491 images, 98% indexed
  - Rippikirjat, Aa:15 (1839–1849) — image group 102151581, 548 images, 96% indexed
  - Rippikirjat, Aa:16 (1839–1849) — image group 102151582, 539 images, 99% indexed
  - Rippikirjat, Aa:17 (1839–1849) — image group 102151583, 519 images, 98% indexed
- All volumes are in Swedish; none are full-text searchable, but all are highly name-indexed via FamilySearch collection 2805467.
- **Access:** [Finland, Church Census and Pre-Confirmation Books, 1600-1916](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2805467) — indexed + images, free at FamilySearch.

#### Pre-confirmation books (Lastenkirjat / Barnböcker)
- **What they are:** Lists of children who have not yet been confirmed, grouped by household and village. They record the child's name, birth date, parents, and ultimately the date of confirmation or death. This is the key source for children in eastern Finnish parishes.
- **For Elsa Brita Heikkinen (b./chr. 1832):** She would appear in the lastenkirjat for the years covering 1832 through her confirmation (~1846–1848). These volumes should give her birth date.
- **FamilySearch volumes for 1800–1850:**
  - Lastenkirjat, Ab:5 (1790–1826) — image group 102151588, 490 images, 94% indexed
  - Lastenkirjat, Ab:6 (1827–1839) — image group 102151589, 247 images, 95% indexed
  - Lastenkirjat, Ab:7 (1821–1839) — image group 102151590, 257 images, 91% indexed
  - Lastenkirjat, Ab:8 (1839–1849) — image group 102151591, 389 images, 94% indexed
  - Lastenkirjat, Ab:9 (1839–1849) — image group 102151592, 383 images, 98% indexed
- All in Swedish; highly name-indexed via FamilySearch collection 2805467.

#### Marriage and burial registers
- [Finland, Marriages, 1682-1892](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1676970) — index (also at Ancestry and MyHeritage, subscription)
- [Finland, Burials, 1725-1909](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1676971) — index (also at Ancestry and MyHeritage, subscription)

### Census records
- There was no national census in the modern sense during this period in Finland. The communion books (rippikirjat) serve as the census equivalent — they enumerate the entire parish population by household on a roughly five-year cycle and are the primary tool for tracking a family's presence in the parish. ([Finland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Finland_Church_Records))

### Probate and court records
- **Probate (estate inventories, perukirjat):** [Perukirjat, 1722-1864](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/311183) — Kihlakunnanoikeus (Iisalmen tuomiokunta) — browse-only images at FamilySearch Catalog. Useful when no direct vital record is found.
- **Court records (tuomiokirjat):** Multiple cataloged series cover the period:
  - [Tuomiokirjat, 1797-1812](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/307323) — Iisalmen tuomiokunta
  - [Ilmoitusasiat, 1799-1862](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/310511) — Vähä-Savon ylinen tk.
  - [Tuomiokirjat, 1822-1918](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/3152069) — Iisalmen tuomiokunta
  All are browse-only images at FamilySearch Catalog.

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds (traditional Finnish/Swedish system).
- **Land records:** [Ilmoitusasiat, 1799-1862](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/310511) (Kihlakunnanoikeus, Vähä-Savon ylinen tk.) — browse-only images at FamilySearch Catalog. Earlier land records are in the Vähä-Savon tuomiokunta series.

### Military records
- **Relevant period:** The Finnish War of 1808–1809, immediately before the survey period, transferred Finland to Russia. Military records for men serving in Russian-era Finland are held at the Finnish Military Archives (Sotilaslääketieteen arkisto). FamilySearch has no significant military collection specifically for 1800–1850 Iisalmi.

### Tax records
- [Finland, Tax Lists, 1809-1915](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2704794) — indexed + images, free at FamilySearch. Covers the Russian-era population tax. Useful as a substitute or supplement to the communion book census. Also at [Ancestry: Finland, Population Tax Lists, 1809-1920](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/61626/) (subscription).

### Cemetery records
- The Genealogical Society of Finland headstone database: [haudat.genealogia.fi](http://haudat.genealogia.fi/php/indexs.php)
- BillionGraves: [billiongraves.com](https://billiongraves.com/site-map?country=Finland)
- FindAGrave: [findagrave.com](https://www.findagrave.com/cemetery/search?cemetery-name=&cemetery-loc=Finland)
- Physical sexton records for Iisalmi cemetery, if not already digitized, would be held by the parish or the Finnish National Archives.

### Newspaper records
- The Finnish National Library digital newspaper archive: [digi.kansalliskirjasto.fi](https://digi.kansalliskirjasto.fi/search?formats=NEWSPAPER) — covers 1771–1910. Rural parishes like Iisalmi had limited newspaper coverage in 1800–1850; the most useful items would be legal notices.

### Immigration/emigration records
- For the 1800–1850 period, emigration from Iisalmi was minimal. [Finland, Passport Registers, 1900-1920](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/4139415) is outside the target period.
- Moving certificates (muuttokirjat) — found within the church record series — document movement between parishes. These are part of the rippikirjat and the arrival/removal records, not a separate collection for this period.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch (indexed collections) | Finland Baptisms 1657-1890; Church Census & Pre-Confirmation Books 1600-1916; Marriages; Burials; Tax Lists | Free |
| FamilySearch Catalog (images) | Kirkonkirjat 1664-1950; Kirkonkirjat 1747-1870; court and probate series | Free (some image-only at FamilySearch Centers) |
| Finnish National Archives — ASTIA | All Lutheran parish records 1527 to ~100 years ago, including Iisalmi | Free |
| Digihakemisto | Church record images | Free |
| SSHY / Digiarkisto | Church record images | Free |
| HisKi (Genealogical Society of Finland) | Partial index of Iisalmi births, marriages, burials | Free |

## Records NOT online
- **Orthodox congregation records** — FamilySearch does not hold records from the Iisalmi Orthodox congregation. Contact the Orthodox Diocese of Kuopio and Karelia.
- **Original parish register images via the indexed FamilySearch baptism collection (1778464)** — the collection is an index only. Images must be retrieved from FamilySearch Catalog, ASTIA, Digihakemisto, or SSHY.
- **Military service records for 1800–1850 era** — not covered by any significant FamilySearch collection for this period and place.

## Known record losses
- No specific record destruction events for Iisalmi parish have been identified in the tool results or wiki pages returned. The surviving record series begins in 1657 and runs continuously through the target period. The FamilySearch wiki page and volume_search results show no gaps in coverage for 1800–1850.

## Research tips

- **Start with the baptism index, then go directly to the images.** Search [Finland Baptisms, 1657-1890](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1778464) for Elsa Brita Heikkinen to find the index entry citing the register volume and page. Then open the original register image (from FamilySearch Catalog entry 4110832, ASTIA, or Digihakemisto) to read the birth date alongside the christening entry. ([Finland Church Records — Births and Baptisms](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Finland_Church_Records))
- **Also check the lastenkirjat.** Because Iisalmi is in eastern Finland, Elsa Brita would be listed in the pre-confirmation books from roughly 1832 until confirmation (~1846–1848). These books list her birth date beside her name. Collection 2805467 covers these and is indexed + images. ([Finland, Church Census and Pre-Confirmation Books — FamilySearch Historical Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Finland,_Church_Census_and_Pre-Confirmation_Books_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records))
- **Then search the communion books.** Once Elsa is confirmed, she appears in the rippikirjat with parents' data, birth date, and birthplace alongside her. This is often the clearest statement of the birth date and village. ([Finland Research Tips and Strategies](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Finland_Research_Tips_and_Strategies))
- **Try the HisKi index** as a quick free check: [hiski.genealogia.fi/hiski/205zdi?en+0112](https://hiski.genealogia.fi/hiski/205zdi?en+0112). It is incomplete, so a negative result does not rule out the record.
- **Records are in Swedish.** The surname Heikkinen appears in 1832 records as "Heickin" or similar; the mother's surname Pardanen appears as "Pardain." When searching by name, try both Finnish and Swedish-abbreviated forms. ([Finland Naming Customs](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Finland_Naming_Customs))
- **Eastern Finnish fixed surnames:** Heikkinen is an eastern Finnish family surname (fixed, ending in -nen). All members of the family share the same surname across generations — it is not a patronymic. ([Finland Naming Customs](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Finland_Naming_Customs))
- **If the village of residence is known, it narrows the search significantly.** The communion books and pre-confirmation books are organized by village and farm, not alphabetically. Knowing whether the family was in Kotikylä, Taipale, Soinlahti, or another of the Iisalmi villages allows you to go directly to that section of the register. ([Iisalmi Parish, Kuopio, Finland Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Iisalmi_Parish,_Kuopio,_Finland_Genealogy))
- **Lapinlahti split (1821):** If the family lived in the area that became Lapinlahti parish, check Lapinlahti records from 1821 onward and Iisalmi records before that date. The surrounding parishes (Vierema, Sonkajärvi, Lapinlahti, Maaninka, Pielavesi, Kiuruvesi) should also be searched if the family is near a boundary. ([Iisalmi Parish, Kuopio, Finland Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Iisalmi_Parish,_Kuopio,_Finland_Genealogy))
- **Witnesses in the christening register** often lived nearby and may be relatives. Recording all witness names and residences can help trace the family's network across villages and parishes. ([Finland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Finland_Church_Records))
- **The FamilySearch Finland handwriting guide** will help read the old Swedish-script registers: [Finland Handwriting](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Finland_Handwriting).
